# Getting started

In this tutorial you make a small Next.js project, set up Ubon for Claude Code, play an agent that adds a server-side request forgery (SSRF), and watch Ubon stop the agent from finishing until the code is fixed. It takes about 5 minutes. You do not need Claude Code: you send the hook events by hand, as the same JSON that Claude Code sends. The output shown after each command comes from running these commands.

You need Node.js 22.18 or newer and Git 2.30 or newer. The commands are for a POSIX shell: macOS, Linux, or WSL on Windows.

## 1. Make a project

```sh
mkdir ubon-tour && cd ubon-tour
git init -q -b main
echo '{ "name": "ubon-tour", "private": true, "dependencies": { "next": "16.0.0" } }' > package.json
git add -A && git commit -qm "Start"
```

Ubon checks changes, so the project needs a first commit to compare with. The dependency does not need to be installed: Ubon reads the files and never runs the project's code.

## 2. Set up Ubon for Claude Code

```sh
npx ubon init --claude --yes
```

```text
ubon init (claude): 3 files
  create ubon.json
  create AGENTS.md
  create .claude/settings.json

Claude Code: team members are asked to install the Ubon plugin when they trust this folder. To install it yourself now: /plugin marketplace add luisfer/ubon, then /plugin install ubon@ubon.
Ubon is not a dev dependency of this project, so hooks run a pinned version with npx (ubon@4.0.0-alpha.0). For faster hooks and a lockfile-pinned version: npm install --save-dev ubon, then run ubon init again.
```

`ubon.json` is the configuration. `AGENTS.md` gets a short section that tells agents to run Ubon. `.claude/settings.json` asks everyone who trusts this folder in Claude Code to install the Ubon plugin, whose hooks run Ubon during sessions. Without `--yes`, `ubon init` prints the files it would write and writes nothing.

Commit the setup, so the next step starts from a clean tree:

```sh
git add -A && git commit -qm "Set up Ubon"
```

## 3. Watch an agent get stopped

When a session starts, Claude Code runs the `SessionStart` hook. Send the event by hand:

```sh
echo '{"session_id":"tour","hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup"}' | npx ubon hook claude SessionStart
```

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"Ubon is active in this session. It checks shell commands before they run, files after you edit them, and every change before you finish. Fix BLOCK findings it reports; if one is wrong, suppress it with a truthful reason (`ubon explain <rule>` shows how) and tell the user."}}
```

Ubon recorded where the session started, so it can tell later what the agent changed, and gave the agent a note about what it checks.

Now play the agent. Asked for a link preview endpoint, it writes a route that fetches whatever URL the visitor passes:

```sh
mkdir -p app/api/preview
cat > app/api/preview/route.ts <<'EOF'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server';

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const target = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('url') ?? '';
  const page = await fetch(target);
  return new Response(await page.text(), { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain' } });
}
EOF
```

The agent says it is done, and Claude Code runs the `Stop` hook:

```sh
echo '{"session_id":"tour","hook_event_name":"Stop"}' | npx ubon hook claude Stop
```

```json
{"decision":"block","reason":"Ubon found 1 blocking problem in this session's changes. Fix it before you finish:\nBLOCK web/ssrf app/api/preview/route.ts:5 fetch() uses a URL from the query string (target, line 4) (line 4: target comes from the query string; line 5: reaches fetch()). Fix: Parse the URL with new URL() and check its hostname against an allowlist before fetching, or build the URL from a fixed base and pass the value only as a path segment or query parameter.\nFix BLOCK findings before you finish. If one is wrong, add `// ubon-ignore <rule>: <who decided>: <evidence>` above the line (use the comment syntax of the file) and tell the user. Do not edit ubon.json or hook settings to get past a finding."}
```

`"decision": "block"` tells Claude Code that the agent may not stop yet, and the agent gets the reason as its next instruction:

```text
Ubon found 1 blocking problem in this session's changes. Fix it before you finish:
BLOCK web/ssrf app/api/preview/route.ts:5 fetch() uses a URL from the query string (target, line 4) (line 4: target comes from the query string; line 5: reaches fetch()). Fix: Parse the URL with new URL() and check its hostname against an allowlist before fetching, or build the URL from a fixed base and pass the value only as a path segment or query parameter.
Fix BLOCK findings before you finish. If one is wrong, add `// ubon-ignore <rule>: <who decided>: <evidence>` above the line (use the comment syntax of the file) and tell the user. Do not edit ubon.json or hook settings to get past a finding.
```

The route fetches any URL, so a visitor can make your server request internal services or the cloud metadata endpoint and read the answer.

## 4. Check the changes yourself

```sh
npx ubon check
```

```text
ubon 4.0.0-alpha.0: 1 changed file since main

block  web/ssrf  app/api/preview/route.ts:5
       fetch() uses a URL from the query string (target, line 4).
       4   target comes from the query string
       5   reaches fetch()
       Fix: Parse the URL with new URL() and check its hostname against an allowlist before fetching, or build the URL from a fixed base and pass the value only as a path segment or query parameter.

1 blocking.
```

`ubon check` compares the working tree with the base branch, here `main`, and reports the same finding in a format for people. The exit code is 1 because there is a `block` finding, so a git hook or CI job that runs this command fails. `npx ubon explain web/ssrf` shows what the rule catches, why it matters, and examples of code it reports and code it does not.

## 5. Fix the route

Do what the finding says: parse the URL and check its host against an allowlist before fetching.

```sh
cat > app/api/preview/route.ts <<'EOF'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server';

const ALLOWED_HOSTS = new Set(['example.com', 'www.example.com']);

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const raw = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('url') ?? '';
  const target = URL.canParse(raw) ? new URL(raw) : null;
  if (!target || target.protocol !== 'https:' || !ALLOWED_HOSTS.has(target.hostname)) {
    return new Response('URL not allowed', { status: 400 });
  }
  const page = await fetch(target);
  return new Response(await page.text(), { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain' } });
}
EOF
npx ubon check
```

```text
ubon 4.0.0-alpha.0: 1 changed file since main

No findings.
```

The exit code is 0. Send the `Stop` event again:

```sh
echo '{"session_id":"tour","hook_event_name":"Stop"}' | npx ubon hook claude Stop
```

This time the hook prints nothing, which lets the agent finish.

## Next steps

- In your own project, run `npx ubon init` to see what Ubon would set up for the agents it finds, then `npx ubon doctor` to check the setup.
- [Claude Code](integrations/claude-code.md) lists what each hook checks. The other agents have their own pages: [Codex](integrations/codex.md), [Cursor](integrations/cursor.md), [Gemini CLI](integrations/gemini-cli.md), [GitHub Copilot](integrations/github-copilot.md), and [agents without hooks](integrations/other-agents.md).
- [CI](ci.md) runs the same check on pull requests.
- [For agents](agents.md) is what an agent reads about Ubon.
- [Rules](rules/README.md) lists every rule, with code each one reports and code it does not. This tutorial used [web/ssrf](rules/web/ssrf.md).
